proof_summary: Working p-adically, the proof factors each relevant binomial coefficient into a lower-level binomial coefficient times \(E=\prod_{p\nmid i}(1+N/i)\), and combines a second-order expansion of \(E\) with Wolstenholme-type bounds on \(\sum 1/i\) and \(\sum 1/i^2\) to control the terms whose indices are multiples of \(p\). The remaining indices are grouped into residue blocks and controlled by a recursive descent for weighted inverse-square sums; the two estimates give divisibility by \(p^{3r}\) when \(p\nmid n\), and extracting the full \(p\)-power from \(n\) yields the general case.
